claim: GitHub released a public-preview npm package firewall that intermediates CI and coding-agent downloads, exposing a concrete supply-chain control boundary.
verifiedFacts: GitHub announced October 20 public preview of a package firewall for GitHub Enterprise Cloud customers.
The firewall intermediates package metadata and downloads, with cooldown, advisory checks and attestation-downgrade checks.
GitHub states the preview currently supports npm only and will be metered after the free preview.
inference: Inference: controlled npm install is an actionable safeguard for autonomous build handoffs; no claim Seed Loom already uses this paid feature.
Actors: GitHub provider/builder; enterprise organizations eligible users; GitHub Actions runners and coding agents are protected endpoints.
Consultancy: Dependency Boundary Review for AI-built web systems; client problem is dependency-install risk in CI.
Disposition: qt314wink/seed-loom CORE; MelodicBloom/flore-orthography-memphis-ui PRODUCTIZE; reinforces dependency-provenance thesis.
significance: New first-party supply-chain control gives a concrete benchmark for code-generation and npm build safety.
assumptions: Small teams can obtain comparable controls without Enterprise Cloud.
knownLimitations: Enterprise Cloud entitlement required; preview supports npm only.
Preview effectiveness, false-positive rates and future pricing unknown.
